Thanks Ben. I pulled the workbook and ran three quick scenarios against our 80B-class baseline model (FP16, kv-cache warm). High level findings and recommended commitments: 

Summary numbers (rounded):
- Customer-stated peak tokens/sec: 65,000 tokens/sec.
- Baseline per-GPU sustainable tokens/sec (p95 latency <=350ms): ~10k tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv using our optimized kernel set for that sequence length distribution.
- Therefore raw capacity required: 7 GPUs to meet peak (65k / 10k = 6.5), round up to 7.

Operational headroom and burst handling:
- Recommend committed slab = 10 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (7 required + 30% headroom). This gives breathing room for KV warmups, model variance, and small traffic spikes without immediate throttling.
- For campaign microbursts to 3,500 reqs/min: those are request-count spikes; mapped to tokens this is an incremental ~24k tokens/sec for short periods. Our 10 GPU slab absorbs typical microbursts; recommend burst pool policy that allows 2x ephemeral scaling (burst to 20 GPUs) for 10 minute windows controlled by cost/usage triggers.

Latency SLO fit notes:
- With 10 GPUs we estimate p95 at ~320ms in steady business-hour peak. If they enable prefix/KV caching on export paths and use our batching config suggestions, p95 drops ~10-20% for interactive calls.
- If they plan large long-form exports (2k+ tokens), expect export p95 to increase; carve export workloads to a separate queue with relaxed SLO and autoscale rules.

Quantization and model variant guidance:
- If customer agrees to int8-quantized model variant for non-critical routes, compression can raise per-GPU throughput to ~14k tokens/sec => peak fit could drop to 5 GPUs committed, but quantized routes need acceptance testing for quality.

Next steps I recommend we: 
1) Share a simple table mapping tokens/sec -> GPUs for 1x/1.3x/2x headroom.
2) Draft an SLA paragraph that states p95 targets for interactive endpoints and relaxed p95 for exports.
3) Propose a 30-day canary: start with 8 GPUs (commit 8, enable burst pool to 16) and measure traffic shape. If metrics look good after 14 days, increase to committed 10.

I can translate these bullets to a one-page attachable sizing note for Alex and procurement.

Kimberly Park
